methods.title: Midpoint and perpendicular bisector
steps: Open the compass to a radius greater than half AB (shown by the dashed radius).
With the same opening draw arcs centred at A and B on both sides of AB.
Mark their intersections X and Y. Join X to Y.
Mark the intersection of XY and AB as M.
methods.why: AX = BX and AY = BY, so XY is the perpendicular bisector of AB; M divides AB into equal halves.
methods.conditions: The compass opening must be greater than half AB.
methods.objective: Construct the midpoint and perpendicular bisector of AB.

methods.title: Perpendicular at a point on a line
steps: With centre P draw an arc crossing l at A and B.
Using equal openings greater than AP, draw arcs from A and B to intersect at X off l.
Join P to X.
methods.why: PA = PB and XA = XB; PX is the perpendicular bisector of AB.
methods.conditions: Choose an arc intersection away from l.
methods.objective: Construct a perpendicular to l through P.

methods.title: Perpendicular from an external point to a line
steps: Draw a circle centred at P large enough to cross l at A and B.
Construct the perpendicular bisector of AB.
Mark its intersection with l as F. Join P to F.
methods.why: P is equidistant from A and B, so P lies on the perpendicular bisector.
methods.conditions: The first circle must cross the line twice.
methods.objective: Construct a perpendicular from P to l.

methods.title: Bisect an angle
steps: Draw an arc centred at O crossing both arms at X and Y.
With equal compass openings greater than half XY, draw arcs from X and Y meeting inside the angle at Z.
Join O to Z.
methods.why: Triangles OXZ and OYZ are congruent by SSS.
methods.conditions: Use the intersection within the intended angle; the other direction bisects the opposite angle.
methods.objective: Construct the bisector of angle AOB.

methods.title: Copy an angle
steps: Draw an arc centred at O crossing the arms at X and Y.
With the same opening draw an arc centred at P crossing PQ at R.
Set the compass opening to XY. Draw an arc from R intersecting the second arc at S.
Join P to S.
methods.why: The original and copied triangles have three matching sides.
methods.conditions: Choose the intersection on the desired side of PQ.
methods.objective: Construct a copy of angle AOB at P.

methods.title: Parallel through a point
steps: From P draw an arc crossing the given line at A and B.
Construct the perpendicular bisector of AB. It passes through P and meets the line at F.
With centre P mark equally spaced points X and Y on the perpendicular.
Draw equal arcs from X and Y to intersect at Z. Join P to Z: the required parallel.
methods.why: Two distinct lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel.
methods.conditions: The first perpendicular is a construction line.
methods.objective: Construct a line through P parallel to l.

methods.title: Triangle from three side lengths
steps: Draw AB to the specified length.
Draw an arc of radius b centred at A.
Draw an arc of radius a centred at B.
Mark either intersection C and join AC and BC.
methods.why: The arcs enforce both remaining side lengths.
methods.conditions: The lengths must satisfy the strict triangle inequality. Reflections are valid.
methods.objective: Construct triangle ABC with the three specified sides.

methods.title: Triangle from two angles and an included side
steps: Draw AB to length.
Construct the given angle at A using AB as the reference.
Construct the given angle at B using BA as the reference on the same side of AB.
Mark the intersection of the rays as C.
methods.why: The two rays meet at the unique third vertex on the chosen side.
checks: Two given angles and AB match
methods.conditions: Both angles must be positive and sum to less than 180 degrees. Reflections are valid.
methods.objective: Construct triangle ABC with the specified base and angles.

methods.title: Find the centre of an existing circle
steps: Choose three distinct points A, B and C on the circumference.
Draw chords AB and BC.
Construct their perpendicular bisectors.
Mark the bisectors' intersection O.
methods.why: A circle centre is equidistant from all points on its circumference.
methods.conditions: Use well-separated points to avoid poorly conditioned intersections.
methods.objective: Find the centre of the given circle.

methods.title: Tangent at a point on a circle
steps: Draw radius OT and extend its line through T.
With centre T draw equal arcs to mark points A and B on the extended radius.
Use equal compass openings to draw arcs from A and B meeting at X off the line.
Draw the straight line through T and X. It is the tangent.
methods.why: A radius is perpendicular to the tangent at its point of contact.
methods.conditions: There is exactly one tangent at T.
methods.objective: Construct the tangent through T.

methods.title: Two tangents from an external point to a circle
given: circle with centre O and radius r
steps: Draw segment OP.
Construct the perpendicular bisector of OP and mark midpoint M.
Draw the auxiliary circle centred at M with radius MO.
Mark the two intersections T1 and T2 of the auxiliary and original circles.
Draw PT1 and PT2.
methods.why: OP is the diameter of the auxiliary circle, so by Thales' theorem OT1P and OT2P are right angles. Both segments are perpendicular to the corresponding radii.
methods.conditions: P must be strictly outside the circle. On the circumference there is one tangent; inside there are none.
methods.objective: Construct both tangents through P.

methods.title: Inscribe a regular hexagon in a circle
steps: Choose a point A on the circumference.
Set the compass opening equal to the circle radius.
Keeping the opening unchanged, mark B, C, D, E and F in turn, stepping around the circumference; the next step returns to A.
Join consecutive vertices, including the last to the first.
methods.why: A chord equal to the radius subtends a central angle of 60 degrees.
methods.conditions: Keep the compass opening fixed and progress consistently around the circle.
methods.objective: Inscribe a regular hexagon in the given circle.

methods.title: Construct an equilateral triangle
methods.objective: Construct an equilateral triangle on AB.
steps: Set the compass opening to AB. Draw an arc from A above AB.
Without changing the opening draw an arc from B intersecting the first at C.
Join A to C and B to C.
methods.why: All three sides are equal to the unchanged compass opening.
methods.conditions: Either side of AB is valid.

methods.title: Triangle from two sides and included angle
methods.objective: Construct triangle ABC using the given lengths and included angle.
steps: Draw AB to the given length.
At A use the protractor to draw a ray at the specified angle from AB.
Open the compass to the given length AC and mark C on that ray.
Join B to C.
methods.why: The specified angle and two adjacent sides fix the shape and size.
checks: AB and AC have the specified lengths
Angle BAC has the specified size
methods.conditions: The included angle must lie strictly between 0° and 180°; a reflected triangle is also valid.

methods.title: Right-angled triangle from perpendicular sides
methods.objective: Construct a right-angled triangle with the right angle at A.
steps: Draw AB to length and extend its line past A.
Mark X and Y on the line at equal distances from A.
Draw equal compass arcs from X and Y meeting at Z above the line. Draw ray AZ.
Mark C on AZ using the specified length AC.
Join B to C.
methods.why: The equal arcs locate a perpendicular through A; the compass fixes AC.
checks: AB and AC match the given lengths
methods.conditions: Both given lengths must be positive.

methods.title: Construct a square on a given side
methods.objective: Construct square ABCD on AB.
steps: Mark X and Y at equal distances from A along the extended line AB.
Draw equal arcs from X and Y meeting at Z above AB. Draw a ray through A and Z.
Transfer AB with the compass onto ray AZ to mark D.
Using compass opening AB, draw arcs from B and D to meet at C, other than A.
Join B to C and C to D.
methods.why: AD is perpendicular and equal to AB; the remaining equal-length sides close a square.
methods.conditions: Either side of AB is valid.

methods.title: Construct a rectangle from length and width
methods.objective: Construct rectangle ABCD with the given dimensions.
steps: Draw AB to length.
At A draw a 90° ray from AB and mark D using the width.
At B draw a 90° ray from BA on the same side and mark C at the same width.
Join D to C.
methods.why: Both perpendicular sides are equal and parallel, so the fourth side is parallel and equal to AB.
checks: AB and AD match the given dimensions
methods.conditions: Both dimensions must be positive.

methods.title: Construct a parallelogram from adjacent sides and angle
methods.objective: Construct parallelogram ABCD.
steps: Draw AB to the specified length.
At A construct the specified angle and mark D at the given length AD.
Draw an arc centred at B with radius AD.
Draw an arc centred at D with radius AB. Mark the intersection C on the opposite side of BD from A.
Join B to C and C to D.
methods.why: Both pairs of opposite sides are equal by construction, establishing a parallelogram.
methods.conditions: Choose the non-crossing solution; the included angle must be between 0° and 180°.

methods.title: Construct the circumcircle of a triangle
methods.objective: Draw a circle through all three vertices.
steps: Construct the perpendicular bisector of AB using equal compass arcs.
Construct the perpendicular bisector of BC using equal compass arcs.
Mark their intersection O, the circumcentre.
Set the compass to OA and draw the circle centred at O.
methods.why: O is equidistant from A and B and from B and C; therefore OA = OB = OC.
checks: A, B and C lie on the constructed circle
methods.conditions: For an obtuse triangle the centre lies outside it; allow enough workspace.

methods.title: Construct the incircle of a triangle
methods.objective: Construct the circle touching all three sides internally.
steps: Construct the internal angle bisector at A.
Construct the internal angle bisector at B.
Mark their intersection I, the incentre.
Construct a perpendicular from I to side BC and mark its foot F.
Set the compass opening to IF and draw the circle centred at I.
methods.why: A point on an angle bisector is equidistant from its arms, so I has the same perpendicular distance to all three sides.
checks: Radius IF is perpendicular to BC
methods.conditions: Use the internal angle bisectors, not the external ones.
